draft.title: Fission and fusion
card: a heavy nucleus, such as uranium-235, splits into two smaller nuclei. It is often started when the nucleus absorbs a neutron, and more neutrons are released.
two light nuclei, such as hydrogen isotopes, join to form a heavier nucleus. This needs very high temperature and pressure, as in the Sun, because the nuclei repel each other.
Binding energy per nucleon is the binding energy divided by the number of nucleons. It is greatest for nuclei near iron, so these are the most tightly bound.
In both processes the products have a higher binding energy per nucleon than the starting nuclei. The total mass of the products is slightly less, and the missing mass is released as energy.
draft.remember: Fission and fusion both move nuclei towards more tightly bound products, and the difference is released as energy.

a.q: Why does fusion of two hydrogen nuclei release energy?
opts: The product is more tightly bound per nucleon
The product has more mass than the two nuclei
The product has a lower binding energy per nucleon
The nuclei lose their protons as they join
a.why: The helium-type product has a higher binding energy per nucleon than the hydrogen nuclei, so its total mass is slightly less and the difference is released as energy. It is wrong to say the product has more mass, because that would need energy to be put in.
a.clue: Think about what happens to binding energy per nucleon.

b.q: A uranium-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits into two medium-sized nuclei. Which statement about this event is correct?
opts: The products are more tightly bound per nucleon than uranium
The products have a lower binding energy per nucleon
The total mass of the products equals the starting mass
Energy is released because the products are heavier
b.why: Medium-sized nuclei lie closer to iron, so they have a higher binding energy per nucleon than uranium. The products have slightly less total mass, and that missing mass is released as energy. Saying the masses are equal is tempting, but then no energy could be released.
b.clue: Medium-sized nuclei are nearer to iron on the binding energy curve.

a.best: The product is more tightly bound per nucleon

b.best: The products are more tightly bound per nucleon than uranium

problems.detail: Why (a) calls the product of fusing two hydrogen nuclei 'helium-type'. Two protons fuse to form deuterium. Deuterium and tritium form helium-4 plus a neutron, so the product is not a single helium nucleus. The answer is unaffected, but the why should name a real reaction or not name the product.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct. Why (a) loosely calls the product of fusing two hydrogen nuclei 'helium-type', which is not accurate for that reaction.
